newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.S. vetoes second term for Boutros-Ghali.
newsitem.headline: U.S. vetoes second term for Boutros-Ghali.

text.p: The United States on Monday vetoed a second term for Boutros Boutros-Ghali as U.N. secretary-general, the United Nations announced.
All 14 other council members voted for a resolution recommending the 74-year-old Egyptian diplomat for election by the General Assembly.

The vote was by secret ballot and the results were announced by U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa. The United States announced in June it intended to block Boutros-Ghali's re-election, saying the United Nations needed new leadership to implement reforms.
It also says the Republican-dominated U.S. Congress will not provide the money needed to pay off $1.4 billion in U.S. dues to the world body unless Boutros-Ghali is replaced.
The veto may open the way for other candidates to enter the race for a five-year term as secretary-general beginning January 1, 1997.

The council has agreed to give priority to candidates from Africa, on the grounds that if Boutros-Ghali is denied the second term given his predecessors, he should at least be followed by another African.
